lanes.label: Elsewhere in scripture
lanes.range: Topics in other books wired to this one

nodes.t: Genealogies from Adam to Israel
nodes.d: 1 Chronicles 1 lists the line from Adam to Noah's sons, the nations from Japheth, Ham and Shem, the line to Abraham, Abraham's sons through Ishmael, Keturah and Isaac, and Esau's descendants and the kings of Edom.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} say where 1 Chronicles begins its list of names and why a book of history might start there?
ev: Say whose name begins the list (1:1) and whose sons are named in 1:34
Say which sons of Isaac are traced (1:34)

nodes.t: 1 Chronicles: overview
nodes.d: 1 Chronicles opens with genealogies from Adam to the returned exiles (chs. 1-9), tells of Saul's death and David's reign (chs. 10-21), and then David's preparations for the temple, the organising of Levites and officers, and the accession of Solomon (chs. 22-29).
nodes.q: Can {{name}} outline 1 Chronicles in order, from the genealogies to David's death?
ev: Name the three parts: genealogies, David's reign, preparations for the temple
Say how the book begins (Adam) and ends (David's death and Solomon reigning)

nodes.t: The twelve sons of Israel and the line of Judah
nodes.d: Chapter 2 names the twelve sons of Israel and then follows Judah in detail through Hezron, Ram, Amminadab, Nahshon and Jesse to David, with other branches of Judah's families.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} follow the line from Judah to David in 1 Chronicles 2?
ev: List the twelve sons of Israel as named in 2:1-2
Say whose name ends the main line in 2:13-15

nodes.t: David's sons and the line of the kings of Judah
nodes.d: Chapter 3 lists David's sons born in Hebron and Jerusalem, then follows Solomon's line through the kings of Judah to the exile and the descendants of Jehoiachin.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain what 1 Chronicles 3 traces from David to the exile?
ev: Say where David's sons were born and how long he reigned in each place (3:4)
Name some of the kings in the line from Solomon (3:10-16)

nodes.t: Other families of Judah and Simeon, and Jabez
nodes.d: Chapter 4 lists further families of Judah and Simeon. In the middle the text singles out Jabez, honoured above his brothers, who called on the God of Israel for blessing and was granted what he asked.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} tell what is said about Jabez in 1 Chronicles 4?
ev: Say what Jabez asked of God and the result (4:10)
Name the two tribes whose families are listed

nodes.t: Reuben, Gad and the half-tribe of Manasseh
nodes.d: Chapter 5 explains that Reuben lost the birthright to Joseph, lists Reuben, Gad and half Manasseh east of Jordan, notes that they cried to God and were helped in battle, and says they sinned by following other gods and were carried away by Assyria.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain why 1 Chronicles 5 says the eastern tribes were taken captive?
ev: Say what happened to Reuben's birthright (5:1-2)
Say why the eastern tribes were carried away (5:25-26)

nodes.t: The tribe of Levi: priests and singers
nodes.d: Chapter 6 traces Levi through Gershon, Kohath and Merari, the line of the high priests, the Levitical towns, and the singers David set over the service of song, Heman, Asaph and Ethan.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} say who the priests and singers were according to 1 Chronicles 6?
ev: Name the three sons of Levi (6:1)
Say what David set the singers over (6:31-32)

nodes.t: Issachar, Benjamin, Naphtali, Manasseh, Ephraim and Asher
nodes.d: Chapter 7 lists families of several tribes, noting their numbers of mighty men of valour, and ends with Asher.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} name some of the tribes covered in 1 Chronicles 7?
ev: Name some tribes in the chapter
Say what the writer counts for several tribes

nodes.t: Benjamin and the house of Saul
nodes.d: Chapter 8 lists Benjamin's families, and 8:33-40 traces Saul and his sons; the same line is repeated in 9:35-44, where Saul's descendants are listed again.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} find where 1 Chronicles lists Saul's family?
ev: Say who is named as Saul's father and sons (8:33)
Say where else the line of Saul is listed (9:35-44)

nodes.t: Those who lived in Jerusalem after the captivity
nodes.d: Chapter 9:1-34 says all Israel was reckoned by genealogies, the people carried away to Babylon for their transgression, and lists those who first dwelt in their cities: Israelites, priests, Levites, temple servants, with the porters and singers and their duties.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain what 1 Chronicles 9 says about the people who lived in Jerusalem?
ev: Say why Judah was carried to Babylon (9:1)
Name the groups who lived in Jerusalem (9:2-3)

nodes.t: Saul dies at Gilboa
nodes.d: The Philistines fight Israel, Saul and his sons die, and the Philistines strip Saul and fasten his head in the temple of Dagon; the men of Jabesh-gilead bury him. The text says Saul died for his transgression and for not enquiring of the LORD, and the kingdom was turned to David.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain why 1 Chronicles says Saul died and what happened to the kingdom?
ev: Say why the writer says Saul died (10:13-14)
Say what happened to Saul's body and who buried it

nodes.t: David is made king and takes Jerusalem
nodes.d: All Israel gathers to David at Hebron and he makes a covenant with the elders before the LORD; David and Israel take Jebus (Jerusalem) from the Jebusites, Joab leading, and David dwells there; he grows greater because the LORD of hosts was with him.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain how David became king over all Israel and took Jerusalem?
ev: Say who came to Hebron and what they said (11:1-3)
Say who went up first against the Jebusites (11:6)

nodes.t: David's mighty men
nodes.d: The chief of David's mighty men are named with their deeds: Jashobeam, Eleazar, Abishai and Benaiah, three men who brought David water from the well of Bethlehem (which he poured out to the LORD), and a list of other valiant men.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} tell about David's mighty men and the water from Bethlehem?
ev: Say what David did with the water from Bethlehem and why (11:17-19)
Name two of the mighty men

nodes.t: Those who came to David at Ziklag and Hebron
nodes.d: Chapter 12 lists warriors from Benjamin, Gad, Judah, Manasseh and other tribes who joined David at Ziklag and in the wilderness, and then the tribal armies that came to Hebron with a perfect heart to make him king over all Israel.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain how all Israel came to support David as king?
ev: Say what Amasai told David (12:18)
Say why the tribes came to Hebron (12:38)

nodes.t: The ark moved on a cart and Uzza dies
nodes.d: David consults the leaders and all Israel to bring the ark of God from Kirjath-jearim; on the way Uzza puts out his hand to steady the ark and the LORD strikes him. David is afraid and leaves the ark with Obed-edom, whose house is blessed.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} tell what went wrong when David first tried to bring the ark to Jerusalem?
ev: Retell what happened to Uzza
Say where the ark was left and how the LORD treated that house (13:13-14)

nodes.t: David established at Jerusalem and the Philistines defeated
nodes.d: Hiram of Tyre sends cedar and craftsmen to David, who perceives that the LORD has confirmed him king; the Philistines come twice, David enquires of God each time, and God tells him the second time to wait for the sound in the mulberry trees, and the Philistines are beaten.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain how David knew when to attack the Philistines?
ev: Say what David did before each battle (14:10, 14)
Say what sign God gave David (14:15)

nodes.t: The ark is brought up to Jerusalem
nodes.d: David prepares a place for the ark and says only Levites should carry it; the Levites sanctify themselves and bear it on their shoulders with the staves, singers and instruments appointed, and the ark comes to the city of David with shouting, though Michal despises David.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain how David brought the ark up properly the second time?
ev: Say why David said only the Levites should carry the ark (15:2, 13)
Say how the ark was carried this time (15:15)

nodes.t: The ark in its tent and the worship appointed
nodes.d: The ark is set in the tent David pitched; burnt and peace offerings are made, bread is given to all Israel, and Levites are appointed to minister before the ark and praise the LORD, with Asaph and others, while Zadok and priests serve at Gibeon.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} describe the worship David appointed once the ark was in Jerusalem?
ev: Say what David gave to the people (16:3)
Name the Levite chief appointed to sound the cymbals (16:5)

nodes.t: David's psalm of thanksgiving
nodes.d: David delivers to Asaph a psalm: give thanks to the LORD, seek his face, remember his marvellous works and his covenant with Abraham, Isaac and Jacob, declare his glory to the nations, for the LORD is great and above all gods, and his mercy endures for ever.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} tell some reasons David's psalm gives for thanking the LORD?
ev: Find the lines about the covenant with Abraham and the land of Canaan (16:15-18)
Say what the psalm says about the LORD and the gods of the peoples (16:25-26)

nodes.t: The LORD's promise to David's house
nodes.d: David wants to build a house for the ark but the LORD tells Nathan he will build David a house: he will raise up David's seed, who will build the LORD's house, whose throne will be established for ever and to whom the LORD will be a father. David sits before the LORD, praises him and asks that the word be established.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} tell what the LORD promised David in 1 Chronicles 17 and how David responded?
ev: State what the LORD promises about David's seed and throne (17:11-14)
Say how David responds in prayer (17:16-27)

nodes.t: David's victories and officers
nodes.d: David defeats the Philistines, Moab, Hadarezer of Zobah, the Syrians and Edom, and dedicates the spoil to the LORD; the text says the LORD preserved David whithersoever he went, and lists his officers.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} summarise David's victories in 1 Chronicles 18?
ev: Say who preserved David in battle (18:6, 13)
Say what David did with the silver and gold (18:11)

nodes.t: David and Ammon
nodes.d: David sends messengers to console Hanun king of Ammon, who shames them; Ammon hires Syrians and Joab and Abishai defeat them, and David then defeats Syria. In the next year Joab besieges Rabbah, and giants of the Philistines are killed.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain why David went to war with Ammon?
ev: Say how Hanun treated David's servants (19:4)
Say what Joab said to Abishai before the battle (19:13)

nodes.t: David numbers Israel and the plague
nodes.d: Satan provokes David to number Israel, Joab objects, and David confesses his sin; God sends a plague and 70,000 fall. When the angel stands over Jerusalem, David pleads to bear the punishment, buys Ornan's threshing floor, builds an altar and the LORD answers by fire.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} tell why David's census was sin and how the plague ended?
ev: Say what David chose among the three punishments and why (21:13)
Say what David bought and what he did there (21:24-26)

nodes.t: David prepares for the temple and charges Solomon
nodes.d: David declares the threshing floor the site of the LORD's house, gathers materials, and tells Solomon that though he himself shed much blood, a son of rest will build the house for the LORD's name and the LORD will establish his throne for ever; David commands the princes to help.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain why Solomon, not David, was to build the house, and what David prepared?
ev: Say why David himself could not build the house (22:8)
State what the LORD promised about Solomon (22:9-10)

nodes.t: The Levites' duties
nodes.d: Old David makes Solomon king, numbers the Levites from age twenty and above, and divides them into courses to assist the sons of Aaron, as porters, singers and in the temple service, now that the LORD has given his people rest.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain what the Levites were appointed to do under David?
ev: Name the Levite families (23:6) and some of their duties (23:28-31)
Say why they no longer carry the tabernacle (23:25-26)

nodes.t: The divisions of the priests
nodes.d: Chapter 24 lists the sons of Aaron, notes that Nadab and Abihu died childless, and divides the descendants of Eleazar and Ithamar into twenty-four courses by lot, with Zadok and Ahimelech, and lists remaining Levite heads.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} say how David organised the priests?
ev: Say how the courses were assigned (24:5, 31)
Name the sons of Aaron who had no children (24:2)

nodes.t: The singers of the temple
nodes.d: David and the captains set apart the sons of Asaph, Heman and Jeduthun for the service of prophesying with harps, psalteries and cymbals, in twenty-four courses by lot.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain who the temple singers were and how they served?
ev: Name the three families of singers (25:1)
Say how their duties were assigned (25:8)

nodes.t: Gatekeepers and treasurers
nodes.d: Chapter 26 lists the courses of the porters at the gates of the house of the LORD, the Levites over its treasuries and dedicated things, and officers and judges for outward business.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} describe the gatekeepers and treasurers David appointed?
ev: Say what the porters did (26:12-19)
Say what the treasurers kept (26:20-28)

nodes.t: The monthly army and tribal leaders
nodes.d: Chapter 27 lists the twelve divisions of 24,000 men that served the king by month, the tribal princes, David's stewards and counsellors, and notes that David did not number those under twenty because the LORD had said he would multiply Israel.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} describe how David's army and officers were organised?
ev: Say how the army was organised through the year (27:1)
Name the people who counselled David (27:32-34)

nodes.t: David's charge to Solomon and the assembly
nodes.d: David assembles Israel's leaders, says God did not let him build because he was a man of war, chose him as king for ever and Solomon as successor; he charges Solomon to know and serve God, and gives him the plans for the temple, telling him to be strong.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} tell what David told Solomon and the leaders about the house of God?
ev: State what David says God chose (28:4-6) and the condition he gives (28:7-9)
Say what David gave to Solomon (28:11-19)

nodes.t: The offerings, David's prayer and Solomon enthroned
nodes.d: David gives his own treasure for the house, the leaders give willingly, and David blesses the LORD before the assembly, saying all things come of him, and prays for Solomon. Solomon is made king a second time and sits on the LORD's throne; David dies full of days, riches and honour after reigning forty years.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain how David and the people gave to the house of the LORD, and how the book ends?
ev: Say what David says about giving (29:14-16)
Say how long David reigned (29:27) and who succeeded him

nodes.t: Solomon blesses Israel and recalls the LORD's word to David
nodes.d: Solomon blesses the LORD for keeping what he spoke to David his father, that David's son would build the house, and says the place is set for the ark with the covenant the LORD made with Israel's fathers.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} tell what Solomon says the LORD had spoken to David about building the house?
ev: Say what the LORD promised David about the house (8:18-19)
Explain how Solomon says the promise was kept (8:20)

nodes.t: 2 Kings: overview
nodes.d: 2 Kings continues the divided kingdom from Ahaziah of Israel through Elijah and Elisha, the end of the house of Ahab, the fall of Samaria and the exile of Israel (ch. 17), the kings of Judah including Hezekiah and Josiah, and the exile of Judah to Babylon (ch. 25).
nodes.q: Can {{name}} outline 2 Kings in order, from Elijah's last days to the exile in Babylon?
ev: Name the two kingdoms and say how each ends (ch. 17 and ch. 25)
Name Elijah, Elisha, Hezekiah and Josiah and where they appear

nodes.t: 2 Chronicles: overview
nodes.d: 2 Chronicles tells of Solomon's wisdom and the temple (chs. 1-9), then the kings of Judah from Rehoboam to Zedekiah, with attention to temple worship, reform and returning to the LORD, ending with the exile and Cyrus's decree to rebuild the house (ch. 36).
nodes.q: Can {{name}} outline 2 Chronicles in order, from Solomon's temple to Cyrus's decree?
ev: Say that the book follows Solomon's temple and then the kings of Judah
Say how it ends (36:22-23, Cyrus of Persia)
